title: NADABAS Technical Documentation
text:
Start here
NADABAS is the National Accounts Database System used to compile national accounts statistics with Microsoft Excel, VBA, and SQL Server.
This documentation is maintained with the source code. Changes are reviewed in GitHub pull requests and are expected to describe the versioned behaviour of the repository.

title: NADABAS Technical Documentation
text:
Getting started introduces the source layout and local validation workflow.
Export VBA explains how to create a complete text-based export from an Excel add-in.
Import VBA explains how to build a review add-in from the version-controlled source.
VBA security scanning explains the scanner, severity model, and narrow approval process.
Contributing defines the complete contribution and pull request workflow.

title: NADABAS Technical Documentation
text:
Explore the system

Architecture describes the intended component and data-flow documentation.
Database defines the database documentation scope.
Excel integration defines the boundary between Excel, VBA, and external services.
Reference will provide exact, source-verified component and interface details.
Operations will cover administration, diagnostics, backup, restore, and release activities.

title: NADABAS Technical Documentation
text:
Documentation roadmap
The first documentation increment establishes a searchable, reviewable book around the existing developer guides. Later increments will add the system architecture, database design, Excel integration, component reference, operations, and release documentation after each section has been verified against the exported VBA source and supported database versions.
Incomplete material should be tracked as a GitHub issue rather than left as an unowned placeholder in published documentation.

title: Getting started
text:
Prerequisites
NADABAS keeps the exported VBA project, supporting Python tools, tests, and technical documentation in Git. The exported files below vba/ are the source of truth; Excel workbooks and add-ins are build or release artifacts.

title: Getting started
text:
Python 3.12 or newer
Poetry 2.2 or newer
Git and pre-commit
Windows and Microsoft Excel for VBA import and export operations

title: Getting started
text:
Repository structure
vba/
  modules/
  classes/
  forms/
tools/
tests/
docs/
Install the project and development dependencies:
poetry install
poetry run pre-commit install

title: Getting started
text:
Exporting VBA
Export a complete VBA project to a staging directory before copying reviewed changes into vba/. See Export VBA.

title: Getting started
text:
Importing VBA
Dry-run an import and build a review copy from the version-controlled source. The template is never modified. See Import VBA.

title: Getting started
text:
Validate a change
Run the same core checks used by GitHub Actions:
poetry run pre-commit run --all-files
poetry run pytest -v
poetry run python tools/scan_vba_security.py vba `
  --approvals tools/vba-security-approvals.json `
  --show-approved
Read the repository’s contribution guidelines before opening a pull request.

title: Export VBA from an Excel add-in
text:
Prerequisites
tools/export_vba.py exports the complete VBA project from a NADABAS .xlam, .xlsm, or .xlsb file into the repository layout used below vba/.
Close other Excel windows before exporting.
crumbs: 3  Export VBA from an Excel add-in

title: Export VBA from an Excel add-in
text:
Windows with Microsoft Excel installed
Python 3.12 or newer and the project dependencies installed
An unlocked VBA project in the source file
In Excel: File > Options > Trust Center > Trust Center Settings > Macro Settings > Trust access to the VBA project object model
crumbs: 3  Export VBA from an Excel add-in

title: Export VBA from an Excel add-in
text:
Export
From the repository root, export into a new staging directory:
python tools/export_vba.py C:\path\to\NADABAS.xlam `
  --output-root build\exported-vba
The source workbook is opened read-only with macros, events, alerts, and link updates disabled. Components are first written to a temporary directory; the requested output becomes visible only after the complete export succeeds.
The output contains:

standard modules in modules/*.bas;
class and document modules in classes/*.cls; and
complete UserForms in forms/*.frm with their binary .frx sidecars.

Use --force only when an existing staging directory may be replaced. Copy the reviewed modules/, classes/, and forms/ directories into vba/, but keep vba/ReadMe.md.
crumbs: 3  Export VBA from an Excel add-in

title: Export VBA from an Excel add-in
text:
Validate before publishing
Run the unit tests and security scan, then verify a rebuild through Excel:
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python tools/scan_vba_security.py vba
python tools/import_vba.py C:\path\to\NADABAS.xlam `
  --source-root vba `
  --dry-run `
  --replace-form-designers
Exporting does not modify or invalidate the signature on the source workbook. A rebuilt workbook is a new artifact and must be tested and signed separately.
crumbs: 3  Export VBA from an Excel add-in

title: Import VBA into an XLAM
text:
Prerequisites
tools/import_vba.py builds a new NADABAS add-in from an existing .xlam template and the version-controlled files below vba/. The template is never modified.
Close the NADABAS add-in before building if Excel has locked the file.
crumbs: 4  Import VBA into an XLAM

title: Import VBA into an XLAM
text:
Windows with Microsoft Excel installed
Python 3.12 or newer and the project dependencies installed
An unlocked VBA project in the template
In Excel: File > Options > Trust Center > Trust Center Settings > Macro Settings > Trust access to the VBA project object model
crumbs: 4  Import VBA into an XLAM

title: Import VBA into an XLAM
text:
Validate first
From the repository root, run:
python tools/import_vba.py C:\path\to\NADABAS.xlam --source-root vba --dry-run
The dry run opens the template with macros and events disabled, validates the sources, and lists every planned component operation without changing a file.
crumbs: 4  Import VBA into an XLAM

title: Import VBA into an XLAM
text:
Build the add-in
python tools/import_vba.py C:\path\to\NADABAS.xlam `
  --source-root vba `
  --output build\NADABAS-review.xlam
Use --force only when an existing output file may be replaced. The importer works on a temporary copy and moves it to the output path only after Excel has saved successfully.
crumbs: 4  Import VBA into an XLAM

title: Import VBA into an XLAM
text:
Modules, classes, and UserForms
For a component already present in the template, the importer replaces only its code module. This is intentional: it preserves the controls and binary designer state of existing UserForms unless complete designer replacement is requested.
A new standard module can be created from a .bas file. A new class or UserForm must be a complete export when it relies on VBA attributes or form designer data. A new UserForm therefore needs both its complete .frm file and every referenced .frx sidecar.
To apply reviewed UserForm designer changes as well as code, export a complete .frm/.frx pair and build with:
python tools/import_vba.py C:\path\to\NADABAS.xlam `
  --source-root vba `
  --output build\NADABAS-review.xlam `
  --replace-form-designers
Keep .bas, .cls, and .frm files on CRLF line endings. Excel can interpret an LF-only .frm as an ordinary standard module. The repository’s .gitattributes and pre-commit configuration enforce the required endings.
crumbs: 4  Import VBA into an XLAM

title: Import VBA into an XLAM
text:
Suggested GitHub workflow

Export or update VBA source files on a feature branch.
Run the security scan and unit tests.
Open a pull request and review the text-based VBA diff.
Merge the approved pull request.
Check out the approved commit and run the importer against the official NADABAS template.
Open the generated add-in in Excel and run the functional test checklist.
Apply the Statistics Norway digital signature after testing, then publish the signed artifact through the normal release channel.

Editing VBA invalidates an existing digital signature. The generated file must therefore be signed after the import and verification steps.
crumbs: 4  Import VBA into an XLAM

title: Import VBA into an XLAM
text:
Troubleshooting

Excel denied access to the VBA project: enable Trust access to the VBA project object model, restart Excel, and try again.
The VBA project is locked: unlock the project in the template before importing.
Missing UserForm binary sidecar: export and commit the .frx file next to its .frm file.
Code-only UserForm is not present in the template: use a template that already contains the form, or create a complete .frm/.frx export.
Output exists: choose a new output path or pass --force deliberately.
crumbs: 4  Import VBA into an XLAM

title: Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations
text:
Run the scanner
tools/scan_vba_security.py is a static review aid for the exported .bas, .cls, and .frm files below vba/. It reports code that deserves human review; a finding does not by itself mean that code is malicious.
From the repository root:
The default policy returns exit code 1 only for unapproved error findings. Warnings and information remain visible without failing CI. Use a stricter threshold when needed:
Available exit codes are:
Use JSON for CI artifacts or further processing:
crumbs: 5  Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations

title: Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations
text:
python tools/scan_vba_security.py vba

python tools/scan_vba_security.py vba --fail-on warning


0: scan completed and the selected threshold passed
1: at least one unapproved finding met the selected threshold
2: invalid arguments, input, or approval configuration


python tools/scan_vba_security.py vba --format json > scan-vba-security.json
crumbs: 5  Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations

title: Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations
text:
Severity model

error: command execution, process termination, downloads, or deletion
warning: shell opening, WMI/process creation, file writes/copies, automation hooks, synthetic keys, or network/file-system automation objects
info: native API declarations, environment reads, WMI queries, or directory creation

The scanner understands VBA apostrophe and Rem comments. It also masks ordinary string contents for rules that look for VBA identifiers, which avoids matches caused by comments and UserForm captions. Rules that must inspect object names or commands inside strings, such as CreateObject and command interpreters, still inspect them deliberately.
crumbs: 5  Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations

title: Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations
text:
Document a reviewed exception
Do not suppress an entire VBA file. If a finding is intentional and has been reviewed, create a JSON file that matches the exact path, rule, and expected line shape:
{
  "approvals": [
    {
      "path": "vba/modules/InstallMeAsAddin.bas",
      "rule_id": "file-delete",
      "line_regex": "^\\s*Kill\\s+AI\\.FullName$",
      "reason": "Reviewed installer operation that replaces the selected NADABAS add-in."
    }
  ]
}
Then run:
python tools/scan_vba_security.py vba \
  --approvals tools/vba-security-approvals.json \
  --show-approved
Keep the approval file under version control. The line expression should be as narrow as practical so a future change of target or operation becomes a new, unapproved finding.
The repository approval file is tools/vba-security-approvals.json. GitHub Actions loads it explicitly and prints approved operations alongside warnings and informational findings. An approval documents reviewed, necessary behaviour; it does not disable the rule for other lines or files.
crumbs: 5  Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations

title: Scan exported VBA for security-relevant operations
text:
Run the tests
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_scan_vba_security.py" -v
Run all repository tests with the project source directory on the Python path:
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v

title: System architecture
text:
Purpose
Describe how Excel, the NADABAS VBA add-in, workbooks, the database, the Windows registry, file storage, and external interfaces cooperate at runtime.

title: System architecture
System architecture
text:
Evidence required
The final page must be checked against the exported modules, classes, and forms below vba/. Security-sensitive flows must also be checked against the security scanner and operational configuration. Architecture diagrams should be stored as Mermaid source where practical.

title: System architecture
text:
Definition of done

Every component in the diagram has an owner and a linked reference page.
Data stores and trust boundaries are explicit.
No credentials, production paths, or environment-specific secrets appear in examples.
The description names the NADABAS versions it has been verified against.

title: Database design
text:
Purpose
Document the database structures and invariants that NADABAS relies on without including production data or credentials.

title: Database design
Database design
text:
Review questions

Which schema definition is authoritative and version controlled?
Which constraints are enforced by the database?
Which invariants currently depend on application code?
How are credentials supplied without being stored in source or documentation?
What recovery steps are required after an interrupted write or migration?

title: Database design
text:
Definition of done
Every table and field described here must be traceable to a supported schema or a documented observation from a non-production environment. Unverified legacy behaviour must be labelled as such and tracked in an issue.

Adding a decision
Create a numbered record when a decision has meaningful alternatives or lasting consequences. Include context, the decision, consequences, alternatives, status, and date. Later decisions should supersede older records rather than rewriting their history.

title: ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto
text:
Context
NADABAS has short Markdown developer guides and a larger technical draft in Microsoft Word. The project needs documentation that is easy to review with source changes, searchable for readers, and still available as a consolidated document for organisational use.
crumbs: 13  ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto

title: ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto
text:
Decision
Maintain the technical documentation as a Quarto book below docs/.

Markdown and Quarto source files are reviewed in normal pull requests.
HTML is the primary reading format.
DOCX is a generated output, not the source of truth.
GitHub Pages is the intended static hosting platform after the build has been validated in CI.
GitHub-recognised community files such as CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, issue forms, and pull request templates remain in their conventional repository locations.
The existing Word draft is migrated incrementally. Each section must be verified against the version-controlled VBA source and supported database design before publication.
crumbs: 13  ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto

title: ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto
text:
Consequences

Contributors need Quarto to preview or render the complete documentation.
Pull requests can review documentation and implementation together.
The project can publish searchable HTML and produce a consolidated Word document from the same chapter structure.
Rendered output directories must not be committed.
Documentation rendering and link validation should become required CI checks after the initial structure has been reviewed.
crumbs: 13  ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto

title: ADR 0001: Maintain technical documentation with Quarto
text:
Alternatives considered

Markdown files viewed only in GitHub
This has the lowest setup cost but becomes difficult to navigate and search as the technical documentation grows.


MkDocs
MkDocs is a strong option for an HTML-only developer site. It was not selected because consolidated Word output remains useful for NADABAS.


GitHub Wiki
A wiki separates documentation history and review from the ordinary source workflow. It is not used as the authoritative technical source.

title: Glossary
text:
This glossary will grow as the technical draft is verified and migrated.







Term
Meaning




NADABAS
National Accounts Database System.


Add-in
The Excel artifact that hosts the NADABAS VBA project.


Exported VBA
Text-based .bas, .cls, .frm, and related .frx files stored under vba/.


Source of truth
The version-controlled representation from which a review or build is performed. For VBA, this is the exported source below vba/.


Review build
A non-production add-in created from reviewed source for functional verification.


Security approval
A narrow, version-controlled exception for one expected scanner finding; it is not a general suppression.


ADR
Architecture Decision Record.
